detailed_analysis: The measured band set — strongest ~142 cm^-1, plus 395, 514, 636, and weak broad 795 cm^-1 — is the diagnostic Raman signature of anatase TiO2. Reference anatase modes: Eg ~144 (dominant), Eg ~197 (weak, often below detection; consistent with the very weak feature seen near 200), B1g ~399, A1g+B1g ~516 (unresolved doublet), Eg ~639, plus a weaker higher-frequency feature. All strongest three bands (142, 514, 395/636) are explained, and no carbonate/sulfate/phosphate/silicate v1 band appears in 950-1100 cm^-1, which rules out those oxyanion classes. The fit's shoulder components at 135 and 391 do not correspond to separate anatase modes; they compensate for the intrinsically asymmetric, wing-heavy (Lorentzian-plus-anharmonic) lineshape of the strong low-frequency phonons. The large residual excursions (up to ~10x noise) concentrated on the steep flanks of the 142 and 395 bands corroborate residual asymmetry/lineshape mismatch rather than missing chemistry. Centers and FWHM of the true bands are tightly constrained (sub-cm^-1). The main Eg band FWHM (~8-21 cm^-1 depending on which component; the sharp core ~8.5 cm^-1) is broader than ideal single-crystal anatase, which can indicate nanocrystalline domain size or minor non-stoichiometry, though the shoulder-component ambiguity limits how firmly this can be stated. No chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, so this identification is pattern-based only.

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum is identified as anatase TiO2 from its diagnostic band set: dominant Eg at 142.1 +/- 0.01 cm^-1, plus 395.2 +/- 0.06, 514.4 +/- 0.03, and 636.4 +/- 0.16 cm^-1, on a flat baseline (fluorescence fraction ~0.039).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Anatase is the photocatalytically active TiO2 polymorph; unambiguous polymorph identification (anatase vs rutile vs brookite) from the low-frequency Eg mode position and the 399/516/639 satellite pattern is central to catalyst, pigment, and thin-film characterization.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed a nanocrystalline anatase TiO2 phase whose dominant Eg Raman mode sits at ~142 cm^-1 with satellite bands at 395/514/636 cm^-1 and no rutile 447/612 cm^-1 features?

model_type: Sum of 7 symmetric pseudo-Voigt profiles on a flat (constant) baseline; full-range fit (91-1286 cm^-1) via staged Trust Region Reflective least squares. Reseeded 128/141 shoulder+main pair and 375/394 flank+main pair with min-separation >=9 cm^-1 soft constraint. Baseline area fraction ~0.039 (rolling-min estimate) -> flat baseline used, no ALS.

reuse_validity.message: Reused the locked fitting script from prior run 'curve_raman'; R² = 0.9986 meets the acceptance threshold 0.950.
